picture.alt: Outside a building with blue-framed glass doors, on a sunny paved path with green bushes behind a railing, four young people stand close together. In the middle, a young man with black hair, an open sage-green shirt over a red striped T-shirt, black trousers and a backpack strap holds up a photo in one hand and points at it with the other, smiling and talking. The photo shows a food stall: a red canopy, yellow paper lanterns, a cook in a white cap and blue clothes behind trays of round snacks, and a red-and-white striped front. At the front on the left, a girl with short wavy dark hair, round glasses and freckles, a white collared shirt, a purple vest, green trousers and a white backpack leans forward with her hands together under her chin, smiling at the photo. Behind her stands a person with long wavy brown hair, a mustard-yellow sweater vest over a purple shirt and a dark green backpack, one finger at the chin, looking at the photo. On the right, a girl with long wavy dark hair, gold hoop earrings, a bright blue shirt over an orange top, white trousers and a black backpack holds her hands together near her chin and smiles at the young man. Nobody is holding a camera.

picture.alt: An evening show outdoors: string lights, a dark blue sky, lit windows of a building and white tents in the back. On a wooden stage with warm lights and a big drum, a young man with black hair, a dark blue jacket with white diamond patterns on the sleeves, a white T-shirt, a teal sash and black trousers dances with one arm up and the other stretched out, smiling. Behind him on the left stands a second young man in the same blue jacket and teal sash, playing a bamboo flute held to the side. In front of the stage, the audience claps: a girl with long wavy dark hair, gold hoop earrings and a blue shirt; a girl with round glasses, a white collar and a purple vest; and a young man with curly blond hair in a teal jacket, all smiling and clapping. In the foreground, the backs of more heads and raised clapping hands.

lines.speaker: F
lines.traditional: 我的日本室友請我嚐她帶來的納豆，我聞了一下，就說我吃飽了。
lines.simplified: 我的日本室友请我尝她带来的纳豆，我闻了一下，就说我吃饱了。
lines.pinyin: Wǒ de Rìběn shìyǒu qǐng wǒ cháng tā dàilái de nàdòu, wǒ wén le yíxià, jiù shuō wǒ chī bǎo le.
lines.english: My Japanese roommate asked me to taste the natto she brought. I smelled it and said I was full.

lines.speaker: M
lines.traditional: 妳不喜歡那個味道嗎？
lines.simplified: 你不喜欢那个味道吗？

lines.speaker: F
lines.traditional: 那個味道怪得很，我連一口都不敢吃。
lines.simplified: 那个味道怪得很，我连一口都不敢吃。
lines.pinyin: Nàge wèidào guài dehěn, wǒ lián yì kǒu dōu bù gǎn chī.
lines.english: The smell is really strange. I didn't dare eat even one bite.

lines.speaker: M
lines.traditional: 怪？香得很呢！每個人的口味不一樣，我就很愛吃。
lines.simplified: 怪？香得很呢！每个人的口味不一样，我就很爱吃。
lines.pinyin: Guài? Xiāng dehěn ne! Měi ge rén de kǒuwèi bù yíyàng, wǒ jiù hěn ài chī.
lines.english: Strange? It smells great! Everyone's taste is different; I love it.

prompt.speaker: N
prompt.traditional: 男的覺得納豆怎麼樣？
prompt.simplified: 男的觉得纳豆怎么样？

lines.speaker: M
lines.traditional: 下星期的交流晚會，大家都要穿自己國家的傳統服裝。我沒帶來，還是別去了。
lines.simplified: 下星期的交流晚会，大家都要穿自己国家的传统服装。我没带来，还是别去了。
lines.pinyin: Xià xīngqí de jiāoliú wǎnhuì, dàjiā dōu yào chuān zìjǐ guójiā de chuántǒng fúzhuāng. Wǒ méi dàilái, háishì bié qù le.
lines.english: At next week's exchange evening everyone has to wear their country's traditional clothes. I didn't bring mine, so I'd better not go.

lines.speaker: F
lines.traditional: 別去？那個晚會好玩得很！服裝可以跟華語文中心借，不用自己買。
lines.simplified: 别去？那个晚会好玩得很！服装可以跟华语文中心借，不用自己买。
lines.pinyin: Bié qù? Nàge wǎnhuì hǎowán dehěn! Fúzhuāng kěyǐ gēn Huáyǔwén Zhōngxīn jiè, búyòng zìjǐ mǎi.
lines.english: Not go? That evening is great fun! You can borrow clothes from the Chinese Language Center; you don't have to buy them.

lines.speaker: M
lines.traditional: 真的嗎？那我明天就去報名。
lines.simplified: 真的吗？那我明天就去报名。
lines.pinyin: Zhēn de ma? Nà wǒ míngtiān jiù qù bàomíng.
lines.english: Really? Then I'll go and sign up tomorrow.

prompt.speaker: N
prompt.traditional: 男的最後打算怎麼做？
prompt.simplified: 男的最后打算怎么做？
prompt.pinyin: Nán de zuìhòu dǎsuàn zěnme zuò?
prompt.english: What does the man finally plan to do?

questions.why: Not going was his first plan. 好玩得很 argues against it, she tells him the clothes can be borrowed, so he will sign up. She says he does not need to buy them.

lines.speaker: F
lines.traditional: 學校在找願意讓外國學生來住一個月的家庭，我們家要不要報名？
lines.simplified: 学校在找愿意让外国学生来住一个月的家庭，我们家要不要报名？
lines.pinyin: Xuéxiào zài zhǎo yuànyì ràng wàiguó xuéshēng lái zhù yí ge yuè de jiātíng, wǒmen jiā yào bú yào bàomíng?
lines.english: The school is looking for families willing to have a foreign student stay for a month. Should our family sign up?

lines.speaker: M
lines.traditional: 得看有沒有空房間。妳哥哥下個月要是搬走了，他的房間就可以給學生住。
lines.simplified: 得看有没有空房间。你哥哥下个月要是搬走了，他的房间就可以给学生住。
lines.pinyin: Děi kàn yǒu méi yǒu kòng fángjiān. Nǐ gēge xià ge yuè yàoshì bān zǒu le, tā de fángjiān jiù kěyǐ gěi xuéshēng zhù.
lines.english: It depends on whether there is an empty room. If your brother moves out next month, a student can have his room.

lines.speaker: F
lines.traditional: 哥哥剛剛說，台中的工作他決定不去了。
lines.simplified: 哥哥刚刚说，台中的工作他决定不去了。
lines.pinyin: Gēge gānggāng shuō, Táizhōng de gōngzuò tā juédìng bú qù le.
lines.english: My brother just said he has decided not to take the job in Taichung.

lines.speaker: M
lines.traditional: 那就等明年再說吧。
lines.simplified: 那就等明年再说吧。
lines.pinyin: Nà jiù děng míngnián zài shuō ba.
lines.english: Then let's wait and see next year.

prompt.speaker: N
prompt.traditional: 他們家最後決定怎麼做？
prompt.simplified: 他们家最后决定怎么做？
prompt.pinyin: Tāmen jiā zuìhòu juédìng zěnme zuò?
prompt.english: What does the family finally decide?

choices.speaker: N
choices.english: Put the student in the brother's room.

choices.english: Move to Taichung with the brother.

questions.why: 得看有沒有空房間: it depends on a free room, and the room only comes free if the brother moves out. He is staying, so the father says to wait until next year.

lines.speaker: F
lines.traditional: 星期五的交流活動要準備吃的，叫披薩好不好？
lines.simplified: 星期五的交流活动要准备吃的，叫披萨好不好？

lines.english: We need food for Friday's exchange event. How about ordering pizza?

lines.speaker: M
lines.traditional: 要看來的同學是從哪裡來的。歐洲同學多的話，就叫披薩；亞洲同學多的話，水餃或炒飯比較好。
lines.simplified: 要看来的同学是从哪里来的。欧洲同学多的话，就叫披萨；亚洲同学多的话，水饺或炒饭比较好。
lines.pinyin: Yào kàn lái de tóngxué shì cóng nǎlǐ lái de. Ōuzhōu tóngxué duō de huà, jiù jiào pīsà; Yàzhōu tóngxué duō de huà, shuǐjiǎo huò chǎofàn bǐjiào hǎo.
lines.english: It depends on where the students who come are from. If most are European, we order pizza; if most are Asian, dumplings or fried rice are better.

lines.speaker: F
lines.traditional: 報名的有十二個日本人跟韓國人，法國人只有三個。
lines.simplified: 报名的有十二个日本人跟韩国人，法国人只有三个。
lines.pinyin: Bàomíng de yǒu shí'èr ge Rìběn rén gēn Hánguó rén, Fǎguó rén zhǐyǒu sān ge.
lines.english: Twelve Japanese and Korean students signed up, and only three French.

prompt.speaker: N
prompt.traditional: 他們最後可能準備什麼？
prompt.simplified: 他们最后可能准备什么？
prompt.pinyin: Tāmen zuìhòu kěnéng zhǔnbèi shénme?
prompt.english: What will they probably prepare in the end?

questions.why: 要看來的同學是從哪裡來的 makes the food depend on who comes. Japanese and Korean students are from Asia and they are most of the list, so it will be dumplings or fried rice. Pizza was her first idea.

lines.speaker: F
lines.traditional: 昨天禮堂的跳舞表演，你看了嗎？
lines.simplified: 昨天礼堂的跳舞表演，你看了吗？
lines.pinyin: Zuótiān lǐtáng de tiàowǔ biǎoyǎn, nǐ kàn le ma?
lines.english: Did you see the dance show in the auditorium yesterday?

lines.speaker: M
lines.traditional: 差一點就沒看到！我把時間記錯了，以為八點才開始。還好朋友打電話來問我在哪裡，我叫了計程車過去，到的時候表演剛要開始。
lines.simplified: 差一点就没看到！我把时间记错了，以为八点才开始。还好朋友打电话来问我在哪里，我叫了计程车过去，到的时候表演刚要开始。
lines.pinyin: Chà yìdiǎn jiù méi kàndào! Wǒ bǎ shíjiān jì cuò le, yǐwéi bā diǎn cái kāishǐ. Hái hǎo péngyǒu dǎ diànhuà lái wèn wǒ zài nǎlǐ, wǒ jiào le jìchéngchē guòqù, dào de shíhòu biǎoyǎn gāng yào kāishǐ.
lines.english: I almost missed it! I got the time wrong and thought it started at eight. Luckily a friend called to ask where I was. I took a taxi, and when I got there the show was just about to start.

lines.speaker: F
lines.traditional: 那還好。
lines.simplified: 那还好。
lines.pinyin: Nà hái hǎo.
lines.english: That's lucky, then.

prompt.speaker: N
prompt.traditional: 男的是什麼意思？

choices.speaker: N
choices.english: He saw the show after all.

choices.speaker: N
choices.pinyin: Tā bā diǎn cái dào lǐtáng.

choices.speaker: N
choices.pinyin: Péngyǒu péi tā qù kàn biǎoyǎn.

questions.why: 差一點就沒看到 means he very nearly missed it, so in the end he did see it: he arrived just as it began. Eight o'clock was only the wrong time he had in mind, and the friend only phoned.

lines.speaker: F

lines.english: I thought that African student had only been in Taiwan for half a year, so his Chinese couldn't be very good. Who knew he speaks better than everyone in our class.

lines.speaker: M
lines.traditional: 他在他們國家學了三年了，來台灣以前就常跟台灣朋友在網路上聊天。
lines.simplified: 他在他们国家学了三年了，来台湾以前就常跟台湾朋友在网路上聊天。
lines.pinyin: Tā zài tāmen guójiā xué le sān nián le, lái Táiwān yǐqián jiù cháng gēn Táiwān péngyǒu zài wǎnglù shàng liáotiān.
lines.english: He studied for three years in his country, and before coming to Taiwan he often chatted online with Taiwanese friends.

prompt.speaker: N
prompt.traditional: 女的是什麼意思？
prompt.simplified: 女的是什么意思？
prompt.pinyin: Nǚ de shì shénme yìsi?
prompt.english: What does the woman mean?

choices.speaker: N
choices.pinyin: Tā zǎo jiù zhīdào tā Zhōngwén hǎo.
choices.english: She knew all along his Chinese was good.

choices.speaker: N
choices.pinyin: Tā zhǐ xué le bàn nián Zhōngwén.
choices.english: He has studied Chinese for only half a year.

choices.speaker: N
choices.traditional: 她沒想到他中文那麼好
choices.simplified: 她没想到他中文那么好
choices.pinyin: Tā méi xiǎngdào tā Zhōngwén nàme hǎo.
choices.english: She didn't expect his Chinese to be so good.

choices.speaker: N
choices.pinyin: Tā bān shàng de tóngxué bǐjiào hǎo.

questions.why: 誰知道 introduces something she did not expect: she thought his Chinese would be weak, and it is better than her whole class's. Half a year is his time in Taiwan; he studied for three years at home.

lines.traditional: 剛才跟我們說「你好」的那個人，我覺得在哪裡見過，可是想不起來他是誰。
lines.simplified: 刚才跟我们说「你好」的那个人，我觉得在哪里见过，可是想不起来他是谁。
lines.pinyin: Gāngcái gēn wǒmen shuō “nǐ hǎo” de nàge rén, wǒ juéde zài nǎlǐ jiàn guo, kěshì xiǎng bù qǐlái tā shì shéi.
lines.english: That person who just said hello to us: I feel I've seen him somewhere, but I can't remember who he is.

lines.speaker: F
lines.traditional: 他是上個月在禮堂吹笛子的那個美國人啊！
lines.simplified: 他是上个月在礼堂吹笛子的那个美国人啊！
lines.pinyin: Tā shì shàng ge yuè zài lǐtáng chuī dízi de nàge Měiguó rén a!
lines.english: He's the American who played the flute in the auditorium last month!

lines.speaker: M
lines.traditional: 對對對，我想起來了，他吹得好極了。
lines.simplified: 对对对，我想起来了，他吹得好极了。
lines.pinyin: Duì duì duì, wǒ xiǎng qǐlái le, tā chuī de hǎo jí le.
lines.english: Right, now I remember. He played wonderfully.

prompt.traditional: 男的一開始是什麼意思？
prompt.simplified: 男的一开始是什么意思？
prompt.pinyin: Nán de yì kāishǐ shì shénme yìsi?
prompt.english: What does the man mean at first?

choices.speaker: N
choices.pinyin: Tā cónglái méi jiàn guo nàge rén.
choices.english: He had never seen that person.

choices.speaker: N
choices.traditional: 那個人記錯了他的名字
choices.simplified: 那个人记错了他的名字
choices.pinyin: Nàge rén jì cuò le tā de míngzì.
choices.english: That person got his name wrong.

choices.speaker: N
choices.pinyin: Tā bù xiǎng gēn nàge rén shuōhuà.
choices.english: He didn't want to talk to that person.

choices.speaker: N
choices.pinyin: Tā wàng le nàge rén shì shéi.
choices.english: He had forgotten who that person was.

questions.why: 想不起來 means he cannot bring it back to mind: he knows he has seen the man but has forgotten who he is, until she reminds him. He says he has seen him before, so "never seen" is wrong.

intro.speaker: N

intro.pinyin: Qǐng tīng yí duàn duìhuà, ránhòu huídá liǎng ge wèntí.
intro.english: Listen to a conversation, then answer two questions.

lines.traditional: 我們說了半天，還是沒決定攤子要做什麼。表演唱歌怎麼樣？
lines.simplified: 我们说了半天，还是没决定摊子要做什么。表演唱歌怎么样？
lines.pinyin: Wǒmen shuō le bàntiān, háishì méi juédìng tānzi yào zuò shénme. Biǎoyǎn chànggē zěnmeyàng?
lines.english: We've talked for ages and still haven't decided what our stall will do. How about singing?

lines.speaker: M
lines.traditional: 表演唱歌的社團已經太多了。我想來想去，覺得介紹台灣的傳統玩具比較特別，還可以請大家一起玩。
lines.simplified: 表演唱歌的社团已经太多了。我想来想去，觉得介绍台湾的传统玩具比较特别，还可以请大家一起玩。
lines.pinyin: Biǎoyǎn chànggē de shètuán yǐjīng tài duō le. Wǒ xiǎng lái xiǎng qù, juéde jièshào Táiwān de chuántǒng wánjù bǐjiào tèbié, hái kěyǐ qǐng dàjiā yìqǐ wán.
lines.english: Too many clubs are already singing. I've thought it over and over, and introducing Taiwan's traditional toys would be more special. We could also invite everyone to play.

lines.speaker: F

lines.simplified: 这个想法不错！可是要去哪里找那些玩具呢？

lines.english: That's a nice idea! But where do we find those toys?

lines.speaker: M
lines.traditional: 我爺爺家還留著很多，我這個週末回去拿。
lines.simplified: 我爷爷家还留着很多，我这个周末回去拿。
lines.pinyin: Wǒ yéye jiā hái liú zhe hěn duō, wǒ zhège zhōumò huíqù ná.
lines.english: My grandpa still keeps lots of them at home. I'll go back and get them this weekend.

lines.speaker: F
lines.traditional: 那我來做海報，邀請大家來玩。
lines.simplified: 那我来做海报，邀请大家来玩。
lines.pinyin: Nà wǒ lái zuò hǎibào, yāoqǐng dàjiā lái wán.

Chīfàn de shíhòu, wǒ fāxiàn Táiwān guònián de fēngsú hěn duō, xiàng yú bù néng chī wán, bù néng shuō bù hǎotīng de huà shénme de, dōu hěn yǒu yìsi. Chī wán fàn, nǎinai ná chū yí dà pán pútáo, shuō shì zìjǐ jiā zhòng de, yòu xiǎo yòu yuán, tián dehěn, ràng wǒ hěn gǎndòng. passage.english: Last Spring Festival I spent at a Taiwanese friend's home. My friend's family were all very generous: as soon as we met they gave me a red envelope, and they kept offering me food. At the meal I found that Taiwan has many New Year customs, such as not finishing the fish and not saying unlucky words, and they were all interesting. After the meal Grandma brought out a big plate of grapes, grown by the family themselves, small, round and very sweet, which touched me. Grandma's New Year dishes were wonderful too: none of the dishes I have had in restaurants can compare with hers.

questions.why: The family give a red envelope at once and keep offering food: they are generous, 大方. A family that keeps urging food on a guest is not 安靜 (quiet); 害羞 is the opposite of how they act; 仔細 is about doing something carefully.
Not finishing the fish and not saying unlucky words are rules people keep at New Year: customs, 風俗. 節目 are shows you watch, and 地區 and 民族 are places and peoples, not things you do.
The list opens with 像 and gives two examples, so it closes with 什麼的: 像……什麼的. 的時候, 的話 and 以後 would make the examples a time or a condition, and nothing would follow them.

All four are sweet fruit a family in Taiwan could grow and serve on a plate; the next clause decides: 又小又圓, small and round, so grapes, 葡萄. A watermelon is round but not small, and a mango and a banana are not round.

Grandma's dishes were 好吃極了, so restaurant dishes cannot match them: 都比不上她做的. 比得上 would make them just as good and 超過 better, which takes the praise away, and 像 says only that they look or taste alike.

passage.pinyin: Shàng ge yuè wǒ qù Ōuzhōu kàn Fǎguó péngyǒu, zhù zài tā jiā. Tā de jiārén bú tài huì shuō Yīngwén, wǒ yě bú huì shuō tāmen de yǔyán, gāng kāishǐ wǒ hěn jǐnzhāng, bù zhīdào yào zěnme gēn tāmen liáotiān. Hòulái wǒ fāxiàn, suīrán yǔyán bùtóng, kěshì yí ge wéixiào jiù néng ràng rén juéde hěn wēnnuǎn. Péngyǒu de māma jiāo wǒ zuò le hěn duō Fǎguó de diǎnxīn, xiàng dàngāo, miànbāo shénme de. Wǒ zuò de bú tài hǎo, tā yě cónglái bù pīpíng wǒ, zhǐshì xiào zhe zài jiāo wǒ yí cì. Wǒ juéde Fǎguó cài hǎochī dehěn, zài wǒ chī guo de dōngxi dāngzhōng, zhǐyǒu Táiwān de xiǎochī bǐ de shàng Fǎguó cài.
passage.english: Last month I went to Europe to visit a French friend and stayed at his home. His family don't speak much English and I don't speak theirs, so at first I was nervous and didn't know how to chat with them. Later I found that although our languages differ, a smile is enough to make people feel warm. My friend's mother taught me to make lots of French pastries, such as cakes, bread and so on. I didn't make them very well, but she never criticized me; she just smiled and showed me again. I think French cooking is really delicious: of everything I have eaten, only Taiwanese street food can match French cooking.

questions.why: The sentence before gives the problem: neither side speaks the other's language, so he does not know how to talk with them at all, 聊天. He is already living in their home, so meeting (見面) is no problem, and nothing has gone wrong to complain about (抱怨) or come up to discuss (討論).
雖然語言不同 sets up something that needs no words, and the mother later 笑著 teaches him again: a smile, 微笑. A joke, a story and a suggestion can all be warm, but each needs the shared language they lack.
Two examples followed by 什麼的 need 像 in front: 像蛋糕、麵包什麼的. 連 needs 都 or 也, 比 needs something to compare, and 跟 joins two nouns, not a list ending in 什麼的.
He cooked badly, yet she never 批評 (criticized) him and only showed him again. She was helping him all along, so 從來不幫我 is the opposite of the story; 邀請 and 觀察 do not fit his mistakes.

He has just praised French cooking with 好吃得很, and 只有 picks out the one thing among all he has eaten that can match it: 只有台灣的小吃比得上法國菜. With 比不上, Taiwanese food would be the only thing worse, which the praise does not lead to; 像 and 不像 only say whether the two foods are alike, not how good they are.

text.traditional: 我在華語文中心打工已經一年了。剛開始，我常常覺得外國學生的習慣很怪：有的同學說話的聲音很大，有的同學跟老師說話的時候不看老師的眼睛。我心裡常想：他們真沒有禮貌。後來中心舉辦了一次交流活動，請各國學生介紹自己民族的風俗，連校長也親自來聽。其中有一位非洲同學說，在他們那個地區，跟老師說話時看老師的眼睛是不禮貌的。我仔細聽了以後才知道，這些習慣在他們國家都很平常，就像我們過年要拜拜一樣。這個活動改變了我的想法。從那天起，看到不一樣的習慣，我不再馬上批評，我會先觀察、先問。我明白了，只有先了解別人的文化，才能真的跟他們交朋友，互相學習。

text.pinyin: Wǒ zài Huáyǔwén Zhōngxīn dǎgōng yǐjīng yì nián le. Gāng kāishǐ, wǒ chángcháng juéde wàiguó xuéshēng de xíguàn hěn guài: yǒu de tóngxué shuōhuà de shēngyīn hěn dà, yǒu de tóngxué gēn lǎoshī shuōhuà de shíhòu bú kàn lǎoshī de yǎnjīng. Wǒ xīn lǐ cháng xiǎng: tāmen zhēn méiyǒu lǐmào. Hòulái zhōngxīn jǔbàn le yí cì jiāoliú huódòng, qǐng gè guó xuéshēng jièshào zìjǐ mínzú de fēngsú, lián xiàozhǎng yě qīnzì lái tīng. Qízhōng yǒu yí wèi Fēizhōu tóngxué shuō, zài tāmen nàge dìqū, gēn lǎoshī shuōhuà shí kàn lǎoshī de yǎnjīng shì bù lǐmào de. Wǒ zǐxì tīng le yǐhòu cái zhīdào, zhèxiē xíguàn zài tāmen guójiā dōu hěn píngcháng, jiù xiàng wǒmen guònián yào bàibai yíyàng. Zhège huódòng gǎibiàn le wǒ de xiǎngfǎ. Cóng nà tiān qǐ, kàndào bù yíyàng de xíguàn, wǒ bú zài mǎshàng pīpíng, wǒ huì xiān guānchá, xiān wèn. Wǒ míngbái le, zhǐyǒu xiān liǎojiě biérén de wénhuà, cái néng zhēn de gēn tāmen jiāo péngyǒu, hùxiāng xuéxí.
text.english: I have worked part-time at the Chinese Language Center for a year. At first I often found the foreign students' habits strange: some spoke very loudly, some didn't look the teacher in the eye when talking to them. I often thought to myself: how rude they are. Then the Center held an exchange event and asked students from each country to introduce their own people's customs, and even the principal came in person to listen. One of them, an African student, said that in his region looking a teacher in the eye while talking is rude. Only after listening carefully did I understand that these habits are ordinary in their countries, just as we pray at New Year. The event changed my thinking. From that day on, when I see a different habit I no longer criticize at once; I first watch and ask. I have understood that only by first understanding other people's culture can you really make friends with them and learn from each other.

text.traditional: 我的室友是法國人，下個月就要回國了。我想送她一個有特別意義的禮物，就先問了班上同學的意見。有人推薦台灣茶，有人說可以送平板，可是平板太貴了，茶她又不常喝。我想了很久，覺得買的東西都不如自己做的值得紀念。所以，我用我們這一年的照片做了一部影片，從第一次見面到一起去夜市、一起過春節。影片的內容都是這一年當中我們一起做過的事。不管多忙，我每天晚上都做一點。送她影片那天，她一邊看一邊笑，眼睛都紅了，看得出來她非常感動。她說，除了家人，從來沒有人送過她這樣的禮物。
text.simplified: 我的室友是法国人，下个月就要回国了。我想送她一个有特别意义的礼物，就先问了班上同学的意见。有人推荐台湾茶，有人说可以送平板，可是平板太贵了，茶她又不常喝。我想了很久，觉得买的东西都不如自己做的值得纪念。所以，我用我们这一年的照片做了一部影片，从第一次见面到一起去夜市、一起过春节。影片的内容都是这一年当中我们一起做过的事。不管多忙，我每天晚上都做一点。送她影片那天，她一边看一边笑，眼睛都红了，看得出来她非常感动。她说，除了家人，从来没有人送过她这样的礼物。
text.pinyin: Wǒ de shìyǒu shì Fǎguó rén, xià ge yuè jiù yào huí guó le. Wǒ xiǎng sòng tā yí ge yǒu tèbié yìyì de lǐwù, jiù xiān wèn le bān shàng tóngxué de yìjiàn. Yǒu rén tuījiàn Táiwān chá, yǒu rén shuō kěyǐ sòng píngbǎn, kěshì píngbǎn tài guì le, chá tā yòu bù cháng hē. Wǒ xiǎng le hěn jiǔ, juéde mǎi de dōngxi dōu bùrú zìjǐ zuò de zhídé jìniàn. Suǒyǐ, wǒ yòng wǒmen zhè yì nián de zhàopiàn zuò le yí bù yǐngpiàn, cóng dì yī cì jiànmiàn dào yìqǐ qù yèshì, yìqǐ guò Chūnjié. Yǐngpiàn de nèiróng dōu shì zhè yì nián dāngzhōng wǒmen yìqǐ zuò guo de shì. Bùguǎn duō máng, wǒ měi tiān wǎnshàng dōu zuò yìdiǎn. Sòng tā yǐngpiàn nà tiān, tā yìbiān kàn yìbiān xiào, yǎnjīng dōu hóng le, kàn de chūlái tā fēicháng gǎndòng. Tā shuō, chúle jiārén, cónglái méiyǒu rén sòng guo tā zhèyàng de lǐwù.
text.english: My roommate is French and goes home next month. I wanted to give her a present with special meaning, so first I asked my classmates what they thought. Some recommended Taiwanese tea, some said a tablet, but a tablet was too expensive and she doesn't often drink tea. After thinking for a long time, I felt that nothing bought is as worth keeping as something you make yourself. So I made our photos from this year into a video, from the first time we met to going to night markets and spending Spring Festival together. Everything in it was something we had done together that year. However busy I was, I worked on it a little every evening. The day I gave her the video, she laughed as she watched and her eyes went red; you could see she was deeply moved. She said that apart from her family, nobody had ever given her a present like this.

text.traditional: 上個週末，我跟幾位不同國家的同學坐火車去花蓮。出發那天早上，台北的天氣好極了，大家都很興奮。誰知道一到花蓮，就忽然下起大雨來，我們只好走進火車站附近的一家小吃店，等雨停。店裡的老闆是一位老太太，她看我們是外國人，就親自教我們做當地的特色小吃，還很熱心地說明每一種小吃的做法。要不是那場雨，我們也不會認識這麼熱心的人。下午，雨一停，我們就馬上去海邊走走。回台北以前，老太太還送了我們一盒名產，要我們帶回去慢慢吃。這次旅行雖然有一半的時間在下雨，可是我覺得非常值得，比哪一次都好玩。
text.simplified: 上个周末，我跟几位不同国家的同学坐火车去花莲。出发那天早上，台北的天气好极了，大家都很兴奋。谁知道一到花莲，就忽然下起大雨来，我们只好走进火车站附近的一家小吃店，等雨停。店里的老板是一位老太太，她看我们是外国人，就亲自教我们做当地的特色小吃，还很热心地说明每一种小吃的做法。要不是那场雨，我们也不会认识这么热心的人。下午，雨一停，我们就马上去海边走走。回台北以前，老太太还送了我们一盒名产，要我们带回去慢慢吃。这次旅行虽然有一半的时间在下雨，可是我觉得非常值得，比哪一次都好玩。
text.pinyin: Shàng ge zhōumò, wǒ gēn jǐ wèi bùtóng guójiā de tóngxué zuò huǒchē qù Huālián. Chūfā nà tiān zǎoshàng, Táiběi de tiānqì hǎo jí le, dàjiā dōu hěn xīngfèn. Shéi zhīdào yí dào Huālián, jiù hūrán xià qǐ dà yǔ lái, wǒmen zhǐhǎo zǒu jìn huǒchēzhàn fùjìn de yì jiā xiǎochī diàn, děng yǔ tíng. Diàn lǐ de lǎobǎn shì yí wèi lǎo tàitai, tā kàn wǒmen shì wàiguó rén, jiù qīnzì jiāo wǒmen zuò dāngdì de tèsè xiǎochī, hái hěn rèxīn de shuōmíng měi yì zhǒng xiǎochī de zuòfǎ. Yàobúshì nà cháng yǔ, wǒmen yě bú huì rènshì zhème rèxīn de rén. Xiàwǔ, yǔ yì tíng, wǒmen jiù mǎshàng qù hǎibiān zǒuzou. Huí Táiběi yǐqián, lǎo tàitai hái sòng le wǒmen yì hé míngchǎn, yào wǒmen dài huíqù mànmàn chī. Zhè cì lǚxíng suīrán yǒu yíbàn de shíjiān zài xià yǔ, kěshì wǒ juéde fēicháng zhídé, bǐ nǎ yí cì dōu hǎowán.
text.english: Last weekend I took the train to Hualien with a few classmates from different countries. On the morning we left, the weather in Taipei was wonderful and everyone was excited. Who knew that as soon as we reached Hualien it would suddenly start pouring, so we had to go into a snack shop near the station to wait for the rain to stop. The owner was an old lady who, seeing we were foreigners, taught us herself how to make the local speciality snacks, and kindly explained how each one is made. If it hadn't been for that rain, we would never have met such a kind person. In the afternoon, as soon as the rain stopped, we went straight to the seaside for a walk. Before we went back to Taipei, she even gave us a box of local specialties to take back and enjoy. Although it rained for half of the trip, I think it was well worth it, more fun than any other time.
